svg.title: Choose a mechanism for each Syn operation
svg.desc: Private local work uses a database transaction. Authored knowledge with merge-compatible invariants uses signed causal exchange. Shared authority requiring one outcome uses a trusted authority or crash tolerant service under one owner, or a complete Byzantine fault tolerant engine with independent operators. Open validator membership adds a separate Sybil-resistance decision. External anchoring is optional.
svg.text: Start with the promise each operation must keep
Syn consensus review · 23 October 2026 · proposed decision framework
Is this private local work?
Save drafts, observations and queued work in a local transaction. No community vote is needed.
If shared: can independent valid changes merge without breaking the promised rule?
An authored claim can coexist with another claim. An exclusive permission or adopted ontology may need one outcome.
Yes
No
Signed causal records
Verify authorship and dependencies; preserve disagreement.
Use CRDTs only for suitable, explicitly validated structures.
Authentic authorship is distinct from community endorsement.
Choose the authority and fault model
One trusted owner: local authority or CFT availability.
Independent operators: complete community BFT protocol.
Permissions, adopted rules and exclusive resources.
Compare implementations on the same Syn trace
CometBFT reference · Hiero/Hashgraph comparison
Proofs, recovery and operating cost precede speed ranking.
Promote other BFT candidates when evidence warrants them.
Open validator membership is another decision
Define admission and Sybil resistance explicitly.
Public authors need not be validators or token holders.
A peer ID alone does not create voting legitimacy.
Optional external anchor
Retain independent checkpoint evidence when useful. It does not certify truth, authority or data availability.
Explanatory illustration only. This is not an implemented engine, benchmark or certification.
